entities.name: Rigveda
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The oldest of the four Vedas and one of the oldest religious texts in any Indo-European language (c. 1500–1200 BCE), comprising 1,028 hymns (suktas) organized into 10 books (mandalas) totaling over 10,600 verses. The hymns are addressed to deities of the Indo-Aryan pantheon — Indra (king of the gods, storm warrior), Agni (fire, mediator between humans and gods), Soma (sacred plant/deity), Varuna (cosmic order), Ushas (dawn) — and invoke them in the context of Vedic fire sacrifice (yajna). The Rigveda preserves an extraordinarily precise oral tradition: its padapatha (word-by-word) and vikritipatha (permuted recitation) methods ensured text-perfect transmission for over 3,000 years before it was first written down, making it arguably the most accurately preserved text of its antiquity. UNESCO inscribed the Vedic oral tradition as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2003.
